boundaries.evidence: Empty flag products, $\beta_i\in\{0,1\}$ and the empty dimension vector are covered: step 1.1 identifies the flag variety of a zero- or one-dimensional space with a point and step 2.1 computes dimension zero, while step 6.1 records that empty data only remove factors from the compactification.

The rank-zero subbundle case is the reason the trivial line is adjoined: step 4.2 projectivizes W_nu + O, which has rank at least one, and cites the empty rank-zero case of the quotient convention in [F1]; step 6.1 includes zero arrow and zero rank cases.

Flags of dimension at most one give point factors and the rank-one line bundles projectivize to identity maps over their base, as used in steps 2.1 and 4.2; no nondegeneracy hypothesis is imposed in the Statement.

Degenerate incidence data such as W_nu = 0 over the whole flag base and repeated colors are covered: step 3.1 defines the incidence intrinsically and steps 4.2 and 6.1 define the compactification uniformly for every subbundle.

The chart endpoint t = 0 is exactly what requires the adjoined line: step 4.2 identifies the source over the chart t != 0 with X_nu and step 6.1 performs the same identification for the associated model, with no nonemptiness or properness of the chart complement assumed.

AC is assumed in the Statement and used exactly through [F1] (relative Proj), [F5] (projective implies proper) and [F4]; step 3.1 is the only step that consumes properness, and every adapted-basis and chart selection in steps 2.1-3.1 is made on fixed finite-dimensional data.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the relative Proj construction
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]]).
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $E$ be a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_S$-module of locally constant rank $r\ge0$
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Write
$$\operatorname{Sym}(E)=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^d(E)$$
for the symmetric algebra of $E$
([[def-symmetric-algebra-qc-module]]): a quasi-coherent graded
$\mathcal O_S$-algebra ([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]) with $\operatorname{Sym}^0(E)=\mathcal O_S$,
$\operatorname{Sym}^1(E)=E$, generated as an $\mathcal O_S$-algebra by its
degree-one part $E$, and compatible with base change $S'\to S$
([[lem-symmetric-algebra-qc-and-base-change]]).

**Definition.** The **projective bundle** of $E$ over $S$ is the relative Proj
$$\pi:\mathbb P_S(E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S\operatorname{Sym}(E)\longrightarrow S,$$
with the relative twists $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(n)$, $n\in\mathbb Z$
([[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]]). Since
$\operatorname{Sym}(E)$ is generated in degree one, the degree-one part
$\operatorname{Sym}^1(E)=E$ generates the whole algebra, and there is a
canonical surjection
$$\pi^*E\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(1),$$
the **tautological quotient** of the pullback of $E$; it is locally given by
the coordinate sections of a projective space, over an open set on which
$E\cong\mathcal O_S^{\,r}$.

**Quotient convention.** This is the quotient (Grothendieck) convention: over
an $S$-scheme $g:T\to S$, an $S$-morphism $T\to\mathbb P_S(E)$ is the same as
an isomorphism class of surjections $g^*E\to L$ with $L$ invertible on $T$,
and the universal such quotient is the tautological quotient above; the
representing property is proved as [[thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients]].
The associated affine construction is
$\mathbb V(E)=\operatorname{Spec}_S\operatorname{Sym}(E)$; the rank-zero
case below displays its difference from $\mathbb P_S(E)$ over nonempty $S$.

**Rank zero.** If $E=0$ then $\operatorname{Sym}(E)=\mathcal O_S$ is
concentrated in degree $0$, its irrelevant ideal is $0$, and
$$\mathbb P_S(0)=\varnothing:$$
the total space is empty. This is consistent with the quotient convention,
because a surjection $0\to L$ onto an invertible sheaf exists only over the
empty scheme; the affine bundle $\mathbb V(0)=S$ is nonempty whenever $S$ is.

For every $r$-subset $I$ of a basis of an $n$-dimensional $V$, the locus $p_I\ne0$ in $\operatorname{Gr}(r,V)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf A_k^{r(n-r)}$; these loci cover the Grassmannian and have regular transition maps.
The Plucker image of $\operatorname{Gr}(r,V)$ is a closed projective algebraic set in $\mathbf P(\Lambda^rV)$, cut out by the quadratic Plucker relations.
Nonempty projective varieties $X\subseteq\mathbf P^m_k$ and $Y\subseteq\mathbf P^n_k$ have a product, realized as their Segre image, and that product is a projective variety.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every projective morphism in the finite-dimensional
H-projective convention of this page is proper: if $f:X\to S$ factors over $S$
as
$$X\xrightarrow{i}\mathbb P^n_S\longrightarrow S$$
with $n\ge0$, $i$ a closed immersion and the second arrow the projection, then
$f$ is proper. The empty source, the empty base and the case $n=0$ are
included, and no Noetherian, field, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is
imposed.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The quiver has zero arrows by hypothesis; step 1.1 computes $E_V=0$ and the rank-zero incidence, and step 2.1 computes the defect from that data.
The boundary $n=1$ gives a point flag space and zero defect by step 2.1, matching the $n\ge2$ hypothesis under which the defect is positive.
The degenerate cases $n=0,1$ are treated explicitly in step 2.1, and the general rank-zero computation of step 1.1 is exactly the degenerate incidence $W_\nu=0$.
Step 2.1 identifies $n=2$ as the first value with positive defect and the endpoint values $n=0,1$ as defect zero, so the transition boundary of the phenomenon is located.
AC is inherited through the cited incidence lemma in step 1.1; the rank and defect computations of steps 1.1-2.1 are finite and add no choice.

The image of $\pi_
u$ is the single point, and its single fiber is all of $X_
u$, so the defect $2\dim(	ext{fiber})+\dim(	ext{image})-\dim X_
u$ equals $2\cdot n(n-1)/2+0-n(n-1)/2=n(n-1)/2$, which is positive for $n\ge2$; hence this proper incidence map is not semismall. For $n=0$ or $n=1$ the flag space is a point and the defect is zero, so the non-semismall boundary is exactly $n\ge2$, and a general quiver-flag decomposition proof must allow this case.

derivations.claim: In either word the graded flag base is a single point, since the only full graded flag of $V=V_i\oplus V_j$ with one line in each color is $0\subset V_i\subset V$. There are no arrows other than $i\to j$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(V_i,V_j)=\mathbb C$, so $E_V=\mathbb C^h$, with coordinates the $h$ arrow entries. For the word $(i,j)$ the first line is $V_i$, and stability at $r=1$ forces $x_h(V_i)\subseteq F^1_j=0$, so every arrow coordinate vanishes and the subbundle rank is zero; for the word $(j,i)$ the first line is $V_j$, stability at $r=1$ reads $x_h(F^1_i)=x_h(0)=0\subseteq V_j$ and at $r=2$ reads $x_h(V_i)\subseteq V_j$, both automatic, so every arrow coordinate is free and the rank is $h$. These are the rank counts $\sum_{h:i\to j}\#\{(p,q):\nu_p=i,\nu_q=j,q<p\}$ of the incidence lemma [[lem-quiver-full-flag-incidence-has-a-smooth-projective-compactification]], namely $0$ for $(i,j)$ and $h$ for $(j,i)$.

The lemma's compactification adjoins a trivial line to the incidence subbundle, so the line-projective sources are $\mathbb P_{\rm lines}(0\oplus\mathcal O)$, a point over the flag point, and $\mathbb P_{\rm lines}(\mathbb C^h\oplus\mathcal O)$, and the corresponding maps to $\mathbb P_{\rm lines}(\mathbb C^h\oplus\mathbb C)=\mathbb P^h$ are the point $[0:1]$ and the identity $\mathbb P^h\to\mathbb P^h$ respectively. The inverse image of the affine chart $t\ne0$ is, exactly as in the lemma, the total space of the subbundle over the flag point: the point $x=0$ in the first case and all of $\mathbb C^h$ in the second. For $h=0$ both words give the two point maps, so arbitrary multiplicity including the zero case is covered.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the
relative Proj and scheme-properness suppliers. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite loopless
quiver, with arbitrary finitely many arrows between two distinct vertices. Let
$V=\bigoplus_iV_i$ be a finite-dimensional complex graded vector space,
$\beta_i=\dim V_i$, $E_V=\bigoplus_{h:i\to j}\operatorname{Hom}(V_i,V_j)$ and
$G_V=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}(V_i)$. Let $\nu=(\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_m)$ be a word
with $\beta_i$ occurrences of $i$. Let $\mathcal F_\nu$ be the variety of
increasing full graded flags $0=F^0\subset F^1\subset\cdots\subset F^m=V$ with
$F^r/F^{r-1}$ of color $\nu_r$. Then
$X_\nu=\{(x,F):x_hF_i^r\subset F_j^r\text{ for all }h:i\to j,r\}$ is a
$G_V$-equivariant vector subbundle $W_\nu$ of $E_V\times\mathcal F_\nu$. Its rank
is $\sum_{h:i\to j}\#\{(p,q):\nu_p=i,\nu_q=j,q<p\}$ and its dimension is that
rank plus $\sum_i\beta_i(\beta_i-1)/2$. The map $\pi_\nu:X_\nu\to E_V$ is
projective.

Put $\mathbb P_{\rm lines}(U)=\operatorname{Proj}\operatorname{Sym}(U^\vee)$.
Then the bundle inclusion defines a $G_V$-equivariant projective map
$\bar\pi_\nu:\mathbb P_{\rm lines}(W_\nu\oplus\mathcal O)\to\mathbb P_{\rm lines}(E_V\oplus\mathbb C)$
whose source is smooth projective and whose restriction over the affine chart
$t\ne0$ is exactly $\pi_\nu$. The analogous associated-bundle construction over
any finite product of complex Grassmannians formed from tautological bundles is
a projective map between smooth projective varieties, restricting over its
affine chart to the associated incidence map.

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, $k$ a
field, and $F$ a bounded complex of analytic $k$-sheaves whose cohomology is
locally constant of finite rank on a finite complex algebraic stratification.
Fix finitely many algebraic supports and locally closed inclusions to be
respected. There is a finite compatible smooth complex algebraic Whitney
refinement, a projective compactification with its algebraic boundary
respected, and a finite pair of simplicial complexes $(K,D)$ such that
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\cong|K|\setminus|D|$, every open simplex lies in one complex
stratum, and the marked supports are unions of simplices. One can take
$\dim K\le2\dim_{\mathbb C}X$; in particular constant-sheaf cohomology vanishes
above that real dimension. The same construction applies individually to the
compact controlled links supplied by the conical-neighborhood theorem.

On these models, actual ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary
derived Hom, internal derived Hom and local cohomology with a prescribed
algebraic support have bounded finite-dimensional cochain models. Internal Hom
is constructible on a finite complex Whitney refinement. The local link and
support models vary locally constantly along the corresponding complex strata;
thus their cohomology has finite rank there. Every such model commutes with
extension of the coefficient field. Inclusions and supports are chosen in
finite collections for a given construction; no compatible triangulation of
arbitrary algebraic maps or cyclic diagrams is asserted. Perverse dimensions
remain the dimensions of the complex strata, independent of the auxiliary real
simplices.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero, let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic
variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_p\to Z_m$. The maps $q_p:Z_p\to X$,
$q_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=g_1\cdots g_px$, satisfy $q_p\circ Z_\alpha=q_m$ for
every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ and augment $Z_\bullet$ over the constant
simplicial space $X$.

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_m\to F_p$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_m)\to H^j(A_p)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), that $k$ has
characteristic zero, and that a finite product
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups
acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]).
For equivariant algebraic maps between such varieties, the coherent ordinary
six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category
$D^b_{G,c}$:

1. the functors $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!$ are defined on $D^b_{G,c}$, with
   $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, and the tensor and internal-Hom
   adjunction $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$;
2. composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection
   formula and the trace hold, and for a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$,
   $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ the exchange
   $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey
   Cartesian pasting; proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$;
3. the normalized dualizing object $\omega^G$ restricts to the ordinary
   $\omega_X$ of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]],
   and for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ one has
   $\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$; this is not the unnormalized quotient-stack
   dualizing shift.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). For integers
$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put
$$U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i),\qquad X_N=(U_N\times X)/G,$$
where $G$ acts on $U_N$ by precomposition of frames and on $U_N\times X$
diagonally, and set $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Let
$p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$, with
$P_N=U_N\times X$ and $p_N=(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$, be the
simplicial map of the two action nerves
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]),
and let $Q_N:D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D_c^b(X_N;k)$ be the composite of $p_N^*$ with
the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$
([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]).
Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$ and
   $r\le\min(r_N,r_M)$ the comparison isomorphisms $Q_N\cong Q_M$ on
   intervals of width at most $r$, obtained from the product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M\cong U_{N+M}$, are canonically determined, commute with the
   natural transformations of the construction, and satisfy the cocycle
   identity on products of three resolutions;
5. **trivial group.** If $G$ is trivial then $U_N$, $B_N$ and $X_N$ are $X$
   or a point, $r_N=\infty$, and $Q_N$ is the identity of $D_c^b(X;k)$.

No global tensor splitting
$Ra_{N*}a_N^*B\simeq B\otimes_kR\Gamma(U_N;k)$ is asserted for the
frame-bundle projection $a_N:P_N\to B_N$; the comparison is used only on the
nerve and through the finite local models.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The definition
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]
gives a locally small triangulated category $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with conservative
restriction to $X$ and the stated ordinary shift, and its morphism groups are
computed by the coinduced simplicial injectives of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]. Locally
split free-action descent identifies its finite general linear Stiefel
resolution with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory on $X_N$, and
the bounded Hom and image comparisons, the degree-zero ring comparison and
retract closure of
[[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]]
hold for it. The category is idempotent complete. No derived full faithfulness
of restriction to $X$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the finite general
linear Stiefel resolution
$P_N=U_N\times X\to X_N=P_N/G$ of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]
for $G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ acting on the separated
finite-type complex variety $X$, with base $B_N$, frame space $U_N$,
$u_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}U_N$, $g=\dim_{\mathbb C}G$ and
$s_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}B_N=u_N-g$. Write $Q_N$ for the finite-resolution functor
and let $\operatorname{pr}_X:P_N\to X$, $q_N:P_N\to X_N$ be the two
projections. Then:

1. the middle-perverse t-structure on $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is detected by
   restriction to $X$: for every sufficiently large $N$ and every $a$,
   $A\in{}^pD_G^{\le a}$ holds if and only if the restriction of $A$ to $X$
   lies in ${}^pD^{\le a}(X;k)$, if and only if $Q_N(A)[s_N]$ lies in
   ${}^pD^{\le a}(X_N;k)$, and independently of the sufficiently large $N$;
2. the functor $A\mapsto Q_N(A)[s_N]$ is exact for these middle-perverse
   t-structures and conservative in the sense that $Q_N(A)=0$ if and only if
   $A=0$;
3. perverse truncations lift: for $A\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ and all sufficiently
   large $N$ there is an equivariant perverse truncation
   ${}^p\tau_G^{\le a}A$ with
   $Q_N({}^p\tau_G^{\le a}A)[s_N]\cong{}^p\tau^{\le a}\bigl(Q_N(A)[s_N]\bigr)$,
   canonical up to unique isomorphism, and the family is independent of $N$;
4. at the degree-zero Hom stabilization bound $r_N\ge a-b$ for objects
   concentrated in ordinary degrees $[b,a]$, the ring comparison
   $\operatorname{End}_G(K)\cong\operatorname{End}_{X_N}(Q_NK)$ lifts finite
   families of orthogonal idempotents, and after the common shift $s_N$ the
   normalized functor preserves and reflects perverse concentration and
   simplicity.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero. On the equivariant constructible derived category
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]],
middle perversity is defined on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two
inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and
$H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$, where $i_S$ is the inclusion of a
stratum. These inequalities give a bounded t-structure independent of
compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions,
and the equivariant structure is detected by restriction to $X$. Its heart is
abelian of finite length, and its simple objects are the intermediate
extensions $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)=j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple
finite-rank local systems $L$ on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports
$Z$, with equivariant data in the equivariant category. If $A,B$ lie in the
heart, then $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])=0$ for $m<0$. A simple object's
endomorphism ring is a division $k$-algebra, not asserted to equal $k$.

Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $n$, and let $k$ be any characteristic-zero coefficient field. Then $Rf_*k_X[n]$ is a finite direct sum of shifts of simple perverse sheaves on $Y$; equivalently all its perverse cohomology objects are semisimple and it splits into their shifted sum. This holds without any assumption that $k$ embeds in $\mathbb C$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $U$ is a nonempty
Zariski open subset of a connected smooth complex algebraic variety $S$, then
$U$ is path connected and $\pi_1(U,s)\to\pi_1(S,s)$ is surjective for every
$s\in U$ ([[def-fundamental-groupoid-of-a-space]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every projective morphism in the finite-dimensional
H-projective convention of this page is proper: if $f:X\to S$ factors over $S$
as
$$X\xrightarrow{i}\mathbb P^n_S\longrightarrow S$$
with $n\ge0$, $i$ a closed immersion and the second arrow the projection, then
$f$ is proper. The empty source, the empty base and the case $n=0$ are
included, and no Noetherian, field, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is
imposed.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the uniform all-fibre-open dimension bound $d$ of [[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]]. For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ of locally compact Hausdorff spaces, the proper-support functor $f_!$ of [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]] is left exact, satisfies $(Rf_!A)_y\simeq R\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$ on every fibre, and maps bounded derived categories into bounded derived categories. Its exceptional inverse-image candidate $f^!$ represents the natural Hom transposition $$\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,f^!B)$$ for bounded source objects $A$ and bounded-below target objects $B$, and has lower cohomological bound $\inf(B)-d$. When the later geometric theorem proves that $f^!$ preserves the bounded constructible subcategory, this becomes the right adjunction $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ there; on that bounded constructible specialization the adjunction unit, counit and resolution comparisons satisfy the triangle, identity and cocycle laws. The proper-support evaluation constructs the counit directly. The proof constructs this adjoint from a finite fibrewise-soft resolution and generator complexes, independently of Verdier biduality; it does not infer an unrestricted $D^+$-source adjunction from the bounded-source generator argument.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
